stem:
Acetoin, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(OH)CH}_3$, and diacetyl, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCOCH}_3$, are two of the compounds that give butter its characteristic flavour. Their skeletal formulae are shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Give the systematic name for acetoin.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Identify the reagents and conditions necessary for the conversion of acetoin into diacetyl.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
The infra-red spectrum for acetoin is shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}
parts.text: Explain the main features of this spectrum, with reference to the peaks with wavenumbers greater than $1500\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State and explain how the infra-red spectrum for diacetyl would differ from the infra-red spectrum for acetoin.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
If a sample of acetoin is reacted with concentrated sulfuric acid, a single product is formed that does **not** exhibit stereoisomerism.

However, if a sample of acetoin is reacted with $\text{HBr}$, a mixture of a pair of stereoisomers is produced.
parts.text: Give the structural formula of the product of the reaction of acetoin with concentrated sulfuric acid.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the product in **(i)** does **not** exhibit stereoisomerism.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why the product of reaction of acetoin with $\text{HBr}$ **does** exhibit stereoisomerism.

parts.label: (d)(iv)
parts.text: Draw the two stereoisomers from **(iii)** using the conventional representation.
